title: What to bring home from Zhangjiajie
text: Top souvenirs: Gujang Maojian tea (100-500 yuan), Tujia silver jewelry (from 80), Miao embroidery (from 50), carved quartzite figurines (from 30), smoked sausages (50-100), mountain honey (80-150) and Tu perfume oils (100-200). Bargain hard - first prices are inflated 2-3x.

title: Drones in Zhangjiajie - rules and fines
text: Since 2023 all drones are banned in the park and on Tianmen. Fines 5,000-10,000 yuan plus confiscation. Reasons: safety, wildlife and noise. Flying is only allowed outside the park - over rivers in the city and suburbs at least 5 km from the gates, or with official media permits.

title: Photographing the misty mountains
text: Fog is Zhangjiajie's signature but tricky to capture. Settings: ISO 100-400, f/8-11, shutter from 1/125, exposure compensation +0.5 to +1.0, white balance on Cloudy. Compose with a strong foreground - branch, rock or path - so layers read well. Always shoot RAW for post-processing.

title: Best time to photograph Zhangjiajie
text: Mountain light differs from lowlands. Golden hour sunrise 5:30-6:30 in summer, 7-8 in winter. Blue hour sunset 19-20 summer, 17-17:30 winter. Foggy mornings after rainy nights deliver the iconic Avatar look. Avoid 11-14 - flat overhead light kills depth.

title: Glamping and unusual stays in Zhangjiajie
text: Alternative accommodations for nature lovers: glass houses on mountain slopes with panoramic windows (600-1,200 yuan), traditional Tujia village homestays (200-400), in-park guesthouses at Tianzi Mountain (500-800), seasonal glamping tents (300-500) and cave hotels near Huanglong (400-700).
